lead.headline: Tariff Deadlines, Inflation Data and a Record AI Listing Collide After the Worst Tech Selloff Since April 2025
lead.deck: China exclusions lapse tonight, October CPI lands Tuesday with a December Fed hike priced near 77%, and Russia-Ukraine talks open in Abu Dhabi as a record AI IPO nears its roadshow.

board_note: Figures as of Nov. 5-6 (Friday close/early trading); Sept. CPI is the latest published; sources in each story.

stories.headline: Tariff Cliff Tonight: 178 China Exclusions Expire, Along With Other Truce Deadlines
stories.deck: Unless Washington extends them, the Section 301 exclusions lapse at midnight, the same day several other China-related measures come up for review.
stories.summary: 178 Section 301 China exclusions end Nov. 10; rare-earth suspension and port-equipment tariff delay also expire.
paras: USTR extended 178 exclusions from the Section 301 tariffs on Chinese goods through Nov. 10, 2026, and no replacement date appeared in the sources checked for this edition. If the exclusions are not renewed, the underlying duties would apply to the affected goods again.

A tracker updated Nov. 3 lists other items due on the same date: China's suspension of export controls on medium and heavy rare earths, a delay of a 25% U.S. tariff on maritime equipment, and a delay of 100% tariffs on ship-to-shore cranes and intermodal chassis. Some of the tracker's dates are marked as inconsistent by its own author, so importers should confirm against Federal Register and CBP notices.
Whether the sides extend, let items lapse or trade new concessions is the open question for the week.
money: Importers: check whether your products are on the exclusion list and price in a possible duty increase on shipments entering from Nov. 10; ask a customs broker about timing.
If port equipment duties and rare-earth controls snap back, expect headlines to move shipping, industrial and rare-earth stocks; those names swing hard on trade news.
Buyers of Chinese-made industrial gear may want quotes from non-China suppliers now, before any lapse shows up in prices.
Small sellers who import: hold a cash buffer, since duties are due at entry, not when you sell.

sources.t: USTR extends China Section 301 exclusions to Nov. 10, 2026 (USTR)
Trump 2.0 tariff tracker, Nov. 3 (Reed Smith)

stories.headline: Inflation Test Tuesday After a Blowout Jobs Report Lifts Odds of a December Rate Hike
stories.deck: October CPI arrives with markets pricing roughly a 77% chance the Fed raises rates Dec. 8-9.
stories.summary: 165K jobs, 4.1% unemployment, ~77% hike odds; October CPI due Tuesday.
paras: Employers added 165,000 jobs in October, well above the 65,000 economists expected, and the unemployment rate fell to 4.1%. August and September were revised up by a combined 84,000. Average hourly earnings rose 3.1% from a year earlier. CME FedWatch put the odds of a quarter-point hike at the Dec. 8-9 meeting at 76.8%, which would lift the funds rate to 4%-4.25%.

The Labor Department releases October CPI Tuesday at 8:30 a.m. Eastern. September CPI rose 0.6% on the month and 3.7% from a year earlier, with gasoline up 9.1%; core inflation was 2.6% year over year. Forecasts from the Cleveland Fed nowcast and Continuum Economics point to a smaller October gain of about 0.24% headline and 0.22% core.
One quirk: no October 2025 data exist because of last year's shutdown, so BLS will not publish normal 12-month rates for most October series, and any year-over-year figures are estimates.
money: A hotter reading would likely push mortgage, auto and credit-card rates up; a cooler one could ease them. Consider locking a rate quote if you are in the middle of a purchase.
Credit-card APRs track the Fed, so a hike means paying down variable-rate balances is worth even more.
Savers: high-yield savings and money-market rates tend to rise when the Fed hikes, so check what your bank pays.
Wages of 3.1% are running behind 3.7% inflation, which means real pay is shrinking; that is a reason to ask for a raise tied to the cost of living.

sources.t: US economy adds 165,000 jobs in October (Fox Business)
October 2026 CPI preview (BYDFi)
Preview: U.S. October CPI, a more moderate month (Continuum Economics)

stories.headline: Abu Dhabi Hosts New U.S.-Mediated Russia-Ukraine Talks Tuesday and Wednesday
stories.deck: The agenda covers ending the war and post-war security arrangements; markets will watch for any de-escalation signal.
stories.summary: U.S. envoys mediate Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, Nov. 10-11.
paras: The U.S. is bringing delegations from Russia and Ukraine to Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10-11, with envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner expected to lead for Washington, according to Khaleej Times. Witkoff said the talks will address post-war security agreements, de-escalation, humanitarian measures and ending the war.

Al-Monitor adds that Putin agreed to the round after meeting Witkoff in St. Petersburg and that U.S. negotiators want a breakthrough before winter. Separately, U.S. negotiators planned working-level talks earlier in the week in Brussels with France, Germany, Britain, the EU and NATO. No outcomes have been reported yet.
money: Peace headlines tend to lower energy and European gas prices and lift European stocks; failure does the opposite. Avoid big bets on a single headline.
If you hold energy or defense funds, expect sharp one-day swings around the talks.
Lower oil prices from any de-escalation show up at the pump slowly, so budget for gas prices to stay elevated near term.

sources.t: US to mediate Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi (Khaleej Times)
US to mediate trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi next week (Al-Monitor)

stories.headline: Nasdaq's 5.5% Plunge Gets Only a Partial Rebound as AI Doubts Linger
stories.deck: Thursday's chip-led rout erased trillions in value; Friday's bounce recovered a slice of it.
stories.summary: Nasdaq -5.52% Thursday, +1.09% Friday; S&P 500 closed at 7,376.86.
paras: The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52% on Thursday, Nov. 5, its worst day in 19 months, while the S&P 500 dropped 4.36% and the Dow lost 3.44%, more than 1,800 points. The Nasdaq finished at 24,315, roughly 11.9% below its Oct. 6 record. Reuters estimated S&P 500 companies lost about $3 trillion in value, according to the report.

Reasons cited: doubts about how fast AI data centers can keep being built, midterm results that raised fears of tighter rules and local opposition, a revenue miss at Qualcomm, higher borrowing costs, and questions about how soon AI spending turns into revenue. AMD fell 17.3%, Nvidia 9.3% and GE Vernova 7.5%.

On Friday the S&P 500 rose 0.32% to 7,376.86 and the Nasdaq gained 1.09% to 24,579.42, while the Dow slipped 0.46% to 51,285.73. The VIX, a gauge of expected volatility, fell to 25.49. Over one month the Nasdaq is down about 10.75% and the S&P 500 about 5.45%, per the report.
money: Check how much of your 401(k) or index funds is tied to a handful of AI and chip names; funds that track the S&P 500 are heavily weighted there.
Falling prices let regular monthly contributions buy more shares, but only if you can leave the money alone for years.
Avoid selling in a panic to lock in losses; if you will need cash within a few years, that money generally belongs in safer holdings, not stocks.
Volatility is still elevated, so limit orders beat market orders on thinly traded stocks.

sources.t: Wall Street close, Nov. 6 (Journal Arta)
Why the Nasdaq fell 5.5% (Open magazine)

stories.headline: A Record AI IPO Is Close: Anthropic's Public Filing, Possible Roadshow and a Pre-Thanksgiving Debut
stories.deck: No price range yet, but the paperwork is public and the calendar points to the next two weeks.
stories.summary: Anthropic's S-1 is public (ticker ANT); roadshow could begin Nov. 10; listing reportedly week of Nov. 16.
paras: Disclosure: this briefing was written by Claude, an AI made by Anthropic. The facts below come from outside reporting.

Anthropic filed its S-1 publicly on Oct. 26, with the ticker ANT on the Nasdaq Global Select Market. As of Nov. 5, the price range and share count were still blank; that amendment usually arrives shortly before the roadshow. SEC practice of a 15-day gap after a public filing makes about Nov. 10 the earliest roadshow start, and reports point to a listing the week of Nov. 16, though dates could change.

Valuation is not set. The last company-stated figure was $965 billion in a May funding round; investor talk reported by the Wall Street Journal ranges from $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion, and reports have cited proceeds of $100 billion or more. For scale, SpaceX's June IPO raised a record $75 billion at a $1.77 trillion valuation. FinanceFeeds reports Q3 revenue near $17 billion with a quarterly operating loss of $567 million. Treat all of these as reporting, not company guidance.
money: Retail investors usually get little or no allocation in hot IPOs; first-day prices can differ sharply from the offer price, so avoid chasing at the open.
If you already own index funds, you will likely get exposure automatically once large new listings are added, which is another reason to check concentration.
A giant AI listing can pull money from other tech stocks around the pricing date; know your tolerance before adding to AI holdings.
Read the final prospectus risk factors before investing; the company reports large losses despite fast revenue growth.

sources.t: Anthropic IPO Tracker: date, valuation, S-1 status (Leverage Shares)
Anthropic IPO roadshow looms with no price range (FinanceFeeds)
Anthropic could start IPO roadshow week of Nov. 9 (Implicator)

stories.headline: The Money Calendar: Dates From Tonight Through Jan. 1 That Can Move Your Wallet
stories.deck: Earnings, inflation, a Fed meeting, a funding deadline and open-enrollment cutoffs, in order.
stories.summary: CPI Nov. 10, Fed Dec. 8-9, shutdown deadline Dec. 11, Covered California Dec. 31.
paras: This week: big-name earnings run through Thursday. Reported implied moves include CoreWeave about 21% (Tuesday after close), Hims & Hers about 16% and Trade Desk about 15% (Monday after close), and Applied Materials about 10% (Thursday after close). Implied moves show expected size, not direction. Tuesday also brings October CPI and the China-measures deadline, and the EIA's Short-Term Energy Outlook with new gas-price projections. Russia-Ukraine talks run Nov. 10-11.

Next weeks: Polysilicon tariffs under Section 232 take effect Dec. 4. The Fed meets Dec. 8-9. The current funding law expires Dec. 11, so a partial shutdown would start Dec. 12 without a new bill. Furniture and cabinet tariffs step up Jan. 1.
Personal deadlines: pick a Covered California plan by Dec. 31 to be covered Jan. 1 (enrollment runs to Jan. 31). California's minimum wage rises to $17.40 on Jan. 1.
money: Put these on your calendar and decide ahead of time what you will do if rates, prices or benefits change; decisions made in advance beat headline reactions.
Avoid holding concentrated positions into earnings unless you accept a 10-20% swing either way.
Health plan: compare plans before Dec. 31, not in January, to avoid a coverage gap.
Big purchases of furniture could be cheaper before Jan. 1 if retailers pass on the tariff step-up.

Gas drops to 2026 low ahead of Thanksgiving (Travelers Today)

stories.headline: Iran: Mediators Race a Draft Deal While Tanker Attacks Continue in the Gulf
stories.deck: Talks continue through Qatar, but Iranian sources see a U.S. attack as more likely than a deal.
stories.summary: Iran-U.S. contacts continue via mediators; Hormuz and tanker risk keep oil near $100.
paras: Iran said contacts with the U.S. to end the eight-month war continue through mediators even after talks with Qatari officials ended without a breakthrough, Al-Monitor reported Nov. 2. A draft proposal is circulating. Iran's plan would have the U.S. end its blockade of Iranian ports and cancel new sanctions, with a waiver for Iranian oil sales, while Iran reopens the Strait of Hormuz. Trump said a deal "could happen" but gave no details.

Oil prices fell sharply this week on diplomacy hopes. Brent and WTI dropped about 8% on Wednesday to two-month lows, then bounced as Iran reported three more tanker attacks on Thursday. Brent was near $99.58 early Friday and on track for a roughly 12% weekly loss, per OE Digital.
money: Gas and diesel prices follow crude with a lag; a deal could cut pump prices over weeks, while a strike could reverse the recent dip quickly.
If you drive a lot, fill up when prices dip rather than waiting for a bigger drop that may not come.
Energy stocks and oil funds can swing double digits on war headlines; size positions you can stomach.
Airlines, shippers and retailers benefit from falling oil; consider how much your portfolio depends on either side.

sources.t: Iran says contacts continue after talks end with no breakthrough (Al-Monitor)
Oil heads for steep weekly drop (Offshore Engineer/OE Digital)
Gas drops to 2026 low ahead of Thanksgiving (Travelers Today)

stories.headline: Democrats Take Congress: Shutdown Risk Returns Before the New Majority Is Sworn In
stories.deck: Funding runs out Dec. 11; the Senate has passed none of the 12 regular bills.
stories.summary: Democrats won both chambers; stopgap funding ends Dec. 11.
paras: Democrats won control of both the House and Senate in Tuesday's midterms, and Trump said he would accept the results, which eased political uncertainty, according to Al Jazeera. The new Congress is sworn in Jan. 3, 2027.

The stopgap law funds most programs through Dec. 11; as of Nov. 3 the House had passed 3 of 12 spending bills and the Senate none. Without action, a partial shutdown begins Dec. 12. Most bills need 60 Senate votes. The outgoing Congress could pass a full-year package or a short stopgap into early 2027. Also expiring near that date: the National Flood Insurance Program and surface-transportation extensions.
money: If you are a federal worker or contractor, build an emergency fund covering at least a few weeks of expenses before Dec. 11.
Flood insurance policies could be affected if the program lapses; check renewal dates if you are buying or refinancing a home.
Past shutdowns have had little lasting effect on stocks according to one cited study, but short-term swings are common; avoid reacting to headlines.

sources.t: US markets rise as Democrats sweep midterm elections (Al Jazeera)
The 11 December funding deadline (Multibagg)

stories.headline: Tariff Refunds: A $166 Billion Pool and a Process Still Sorting Out Who Gets Paid
stories.deck: Importers can claim refunds of struck-down IEEPA duties, but timing and eligibility depend on entry status.
stories.summary: CBP's CAPE process covers unliquidated and recently liquidated entries; older entries may be plaintiff-only.
paras: CBP data cited by a customs-law tracker put IEEPA duties paid at roughly $166 billion by about 330,000 importers across 53 million entries. CBP launched the CAPE refund process April 20; Phase 1 covers unliquidated entries and entries liquidated within the prior 80 days, and refunds are generally expected 60-90 days after acceptance.

A Nov. 3 tracker says the government is appealing the part of a Court of International Trade order that requires refunds on finally liquidated entries, and currently limits those to importers with pending cases. The customs-law tracker's own figures are dated early July, so check current CBP guidance before acting.
money: Small importers and sellers: confirm your importer-of-record entries and ask your broker to file under CAPE before the 80-day window closes for each entry.
Check whether your supplier or marketplace owes you a pass-through of refunded duties.
Consider whether you need to join litigation if your entries are finally liquidated; ask a customs attorney.

sources.t: IEEPA refund tracker, CAPE portal status (Great Lakes Customs Law)
Trump 2.0 tariff tracker, Nov. 3 (Reed Smith)

stories.headline: Oil Down 12% on the Week, Gold Up 5%, Mortgage Rates Edge Lower
stories.deck: Energy and rates eased, but gas and borrowing costs remain well above last year.
stories.summary: Brent ~$99.6, gold ~$4,071, 30-yr mortgage 7.18%, national gas $4.10.
paras: Brent crude traded near $99.58 and WTI near $91.38 early Friday, both on track for roughly 12% weekly losses. Spot gold was about $4,070.59, up roughly 5% on the week and its best week in over two months, after hitting a one-year low of $3,869.85 on Oct. 30. Silver was about $52.

Freddie Mac's 30-year mortgage rate fell to 7.18% from 7.24% the prior week, though it was 6.22% a year ago; the 15-year was 6.57%. A separate survey by Mortgage Research Center put the 30-year conventional at 7.046%.

AAA's national gas average was $4.10 on Nov. 5, the lowest of 2026 but about 34% above last Thanksgiving; California averaged about $6.17 in late October. Only about 7 cents of an expected 18-24 cent drop had reached pumps. Goldman Sachs cut its end-2026 gold forecast to $4,150 from $4,650.
money: Mortgage shoppers: ask lenders about rate locks and, if your credit is strong, compare at least three quotes; small rate gaps compound over 30 years.
Drivers: use price-comparison apps; California prices vary widely between stations.
Gold has moved with oil and inflation fears; if you hold it, it is a hedge, not a guaranteed gain.
Falling oil could ease inflation if it holds, but risks remain from the Gulf.

sources.t: Oil heads for steep weekly drop (Offshore Engineer/OE Digital)
Gold stays on track for best week in over two months (Kitco/Reuters)
Mortgage rates edge down third straight week (RISMedia)

stories.headline: IRS Sets 2027 Tax Numbers: Standard Deduction $16,600 Single, $33,200 Joint
stories.deck: Child tax credit rises $100 to $2,300; the top earned-income credit reaches $8,496.
paras: The IRS published its 2027 inflation adjustments (Rev. Proc. 2026-35), as summarized by CPA Practice Advisor. The standard deduction is $33,200 for married couples filing jointly (up $1,000), $16,600 for single filers and $24,925 for heads of household. The 37% bracket starts above $661,375 for single filers and $793,650 for joint filers.

The maximum child tax credit rises to $2,300 (up $100), with up to $1,800 refundable. The maximum earned income tax credit for families with three or more children rises to $8,496 from $8,231. These apply to 2027 income, taxes filed in 2028; the 2026 return you file in spring 2027 uses 2026 numbers.
money: Adjust your W-4 at work if you want to withhold less or more for 2027; use the IRS withholding estimator.
If you expect a big EITC or child credit, ask a free VITA site about filing early next year.
Retirement contributions lower taxable income; check your plan's 2027 limits when they are announced.

sources.t: IRS adjusts tax brackets, standard deduction for 2027 (CPA Practice Advisor)
Projected 2027 tax brackets (CBS News)

stories.headline: Covered California: Enrollment Is Open, With More State Help for Incomes Up to 200% of Poverty
stories.deck: About 200,000 newly eligible people; nearly 200,000 can choose $0-premium Silver plans.
stories.summary: Covered California open through Jan. 31; pick by Dec. 31 for Jan. 1 coverage.
paras: Open enrollment runs Nov. 1 through Jan. 31; to have 2027 coverage start Jan. 1 you must select a plan by Dec. 31. About 55% of enrollees will see no premium increase, 20% pay $0 and 41% pay $100 or less per month, Covered California says.

Federal enhanced premium tax credits expired last year; the state raised its subsidy program funding from $190 million to $300 million, with eligibility up to 200% of the poverty level ($31,920 for one person, $66,000 for a family of four). Help is at (800) 300-1506, closed Nov. 11.
money: Compare plans even if you keep your current one; premiums and networks change.
Check subsidy eligibility; if you earn up to 200% of poverty you may qualify for state help.
Use free certified enrollers to avoid mistakes.

sources.t: Covered California open enrollment 2027 (Covered California)
Covered California open enrollment begins Nov. 1 (NBC Palm Springs)

stories.headline: CalFresh Work Rules Are Live: What 600,000 Californians Should Know
stories.deck: Able-bodied adults 18-64 without a young child must show 20 hours of work or training weekly after three months.
stories.summary: CalFresh work requirement started June 1; current enrollees face it at renewal.
paras: New CalFresh work requirements took effect June 1 for adults 18 to 64 with no disability and no dependent child under 14: after three months of benefits in three years, they must work, train or volunteer at least 20 hours a week (80 a month). New applicants are subject immediately; current enrollees are evaluated at annual renewal.

ABC7 reported more than 600,000 Californians could lose benefits, and about 1.5 million people in Los Angeles County receive CalFresh. Part of program funding shifts to the state. Times of San Diego reports a state lawmaker's office projects about 562,000 people statewide will lose access over the next year, with about 3.4 million households still expected to receive CalFresh in 2026-27.
money: Know your renewal month and keep your contact info current so you get notices.
Short-term training and volunteer hours can count; ask your county.
If you lose benefits, look into food banks and 2-1-1.

sources.t: New CalFresh work rules take effect (ABC7)
As many as 47,000 people could be kicked off CalFresh (Times of San Diego)

stories.headline: AMD -17%, Qualcomm -9%, CVS -12%: The Week's Biggest Single-Stock Swings
stories.deck: Chips led the damage, health insurers and retailers moved on politics, and earnings week brings more.
stories.summary: AMD -17.3%, Nvidia -9.3%, Qualcomm -9.5%; Lucid, CoreWeave report with 20%+ implied moves.
paras: AMD fell 17.26% to $404.40 on Nov. 5 even after beating estimates: Q3 revenue $13.38 billion and a Q4 outlook of about $17 billion, with data-center revenue up 97%. Qualcomm fell 9.49% to $156.75 after guiding profit slightly below expectations and reporting a 26% drop in handset revenue. The selloff was driven by broader AI-infrastructure worries rather than confirmed order cancellations.
This week's earnings include Lucid (about 21.5% implied move) and Hims & Hers (about 16%) on Monday, CoreWeave (about 21%) on Tuesday, and Applied Materials (about 10%) on Thursday.
money: Options-implied moves of 15-20% mean single-stock earnings can cost you a lot; use position limits you can afford to lose.
Beating estimates does not guarantee a gain; guidance and market mood decide.
Own funds instead of individual stocks if you cannot watch earnings.

Why the Nasdaq fell 5.5% (Open magazine)

stories.headline: AMD and Qualcomm Beat or Met Targets and Still Sank: What the Numbers Said
stories.deck: Data-center sales are surging, but guidance on margins and handsets spooked investors.
stories.summary: AMD DC revenue +97%; Qualcomm handsets -26%.
paras: AMD reported Q3 revenue of $13.38 billion against $13.09 billion expected and adjusted EPS of $2.09 against $1.95, with data-center revenue about $8.5 billion, up 97%. Gaming revenue fell 40% and the company guided Q4 gross margin to about 55%. Shares fell 17.26%.
Qualcomm's Q4 handset revenue fell 26% to $5.137 billion while automotive rose 89% to $1.99 billion. Its Q1 guide midpoint for adjusted EPS was $2.25 against $2.27 expected. Shares fell 9.49%.
money: Judge a chip stock by guidance and margins, not just beats.
Gaming and handset weakness shows consumer demand is soft in spots.
Diversify across the AI value chain instead of picking one company.

sources.t: Why Qualcomm and AMD fell (INDmoney)
Why the Nasdaq fell 5.5% (Open magazine)

stories.headline: Big Tech Is Guiding to About $800 Billion in 2026 AI and Data Center Spending
stories.deck: Five companies' capital spending totals roughly $803-828 billion this year, and Q4 outlooks run higher than Q3.
paras: A tally of company disclosures puts Q3 capital spending at $228.3 billion across Amazon ($77.3B), Alphabet ($51.4B), Microsoft ($45.2B), Meta ($34.9B) and SpaceX ($19.6B). Implied Q4 outlooks sum to $241.6-270 billion. Full-year outlooks add up to roughly $803-828 billion by the source's arithmetic.

Alphabet and Amazon said spending will rise in 2027 and Microsoft said it will accelerate in the first half; none gave a figure. The companies use different accounting for leases, so totals are the source's own arithmetic.
money: That spending is revenue for chip, power and equipment makers; but this week showed how fast those stocks can fall when investors doubt the pace.
Check whether your funds hold the spenders or the suppliers.
Do not assume capex means profit; watch revenue growth.

sources.t: Big Tech and SpaceX guide Q4 capex up to $270B (FourWeekMBA)
Why the Nasdaq fell 5.5% (Open magazine)

stories.headline: Marvell's $115 Billion Deal for Lumentum Is the Week's Biggest Merger
stories.deck: An all-stock combination aimed at AI networking is not expected to close until the first half of 2028.
stories.summary: Marvell to buy Lumentum, announced Nov. 2; closes 1H 2028.
paras: Marvell Technology and Lumentum announced an all-stock merger valued at about $115 billion enterprise value on Nov. 2. Each Lumentum share converts into 4.5 Marvell shares. Inside Arbitrage puts that at about $883.80 per share, a 5.13% premium to Lumentum's last close, while Light Reading cites a premium of roughly 23.9% to the unaffected Oct. 28 close. Existing Marvell holders would own about 67% and Lumentum holders 33%; Matt Murphy stays as CEO.

The companies argue AI data-center bandwidth needs and the limits of copper connections are pushing the industry toward optical technology, and they plan to co-design the electrical and optical signal chain. Inside Arbitrage reports the deal is expected to close in the first half of 2028.
money: In stock-for-stock deals, the target's price tracks the buyer's; if you hold Lumentum, you are effectively holding Marvell's risk.
A long timeline leaves room for surprises; do not assume the premium is locked in.
Index and sector funds may shift weights when the deal closes.

sources.t: Marvell-Lumentum merger coverage (Inside Arbitrage)
Marvell strikes $115B deal for Lumentum (Light Reading)

stories.headline: Bitcoin Falls Below $77,000, Down 25% From a Year Ago
stories.deck: A drop of about 5% in a day came amid the broad tech selloff and fresh exchange-hack worries.
stories.summary: Bitcoin ~$76,024, down 5.2% in a day, 11.5% in a month.
paras: Bitcoin was priced at $76,023.87 at 7:15 a.m. ET on Nov. 6, a $4,197.53 or about 5.2% drop from the prior morning's $80,221.40, according to Fortune. It is down about 11.5% from a month earlier and about 25% from a year earlier.

Bitcoin.com News reported that the drop on Thursday coincided with the tech selloff, led by chip stocks, and with concerns about AI infrastructure spending after the midterms. It also cited lingering worries over a $6.3 billion Binance security breach on Oct. 29 and uncertain U.S. crypto regulation, while noting the exact cause cannot be pinned down. Coinglass data in the report showed $838.54 million in liquidations over 24 hours, 88.4% of them long positions.
money: Crypto has been trading like a high-risk tech stock; size positions so a 25% drop would not change your life.
Keep records for taxes: selling or swapping crypto is a taxable event.
Beware of scams promising 'recovery' returns after sell-offs.

sources.t: Price of Bitcoin, Nov. 6, 2026 (Fortune)
Bitcoin price tumbles below $77,000 in tech stock selloff (Bitcoin.com News)

stories.headline: Midterm Winners and Losers: Retailers Up, Health Insurers Down, AI Names Mixed
stories.deck: Markets priced a Democratic sweep on Wednesday; some sectors reacted more than others.
stories.summary: After the sweep: Target +3.3%, Walmart +1.3%, CVS -12%, Nvidia lower at the open.
paras: At Wednesday's open the Dow rose 1.8%, the S&P 500 1.1% and the Nasdaq 1%, per Al Jazeera. Import-reliant retailers rose on the possibility of tariff changes, with Target up 3.3% and Walmart up 1.3%. Health insurers split: CVS fell 12% and UnitedHealthcare 2.9%, while Cigna rose 1.6%.

Tech was mixed: Alphabet rose 3.5% while Oracle and Nvidia opened lower. One analyst cited in the report said Democratic control of the Senate will create hurdles for AI and tech legislation. Brent fell 3.09% to $100.40 that morning. Gains for most were later overwhelmed by Thursday's tech selloff.
money: Opening moves often reverse within days; avoid chasing a sector after a one-day jump.
If you own health-insurer stocks directly, know that policy risk now runs both ways; diversified funds reduce single-company risk.
Tariff relief hopes for retailers are only hopes until a policy changes.

sources.t: US markets rise as Democrats sweep midterm elections (Al Jazeera)
Why the Nasdaq fell 5.5% (Open magazine)

stories.headline: Where Tariffs Stand Now: Section 232 Expands, Section 301 Targets Brazil and Others
stories.deck: New robotics and wind-turbine actions came in late October; a Section 122 ruling is on appeal.
stories.summary: Robotics, wind turbines, pharma, polysilicon: the tariff map keeps growing.
paras: As of Nov. 3: Section 232 tariffs are in force on pharmaceuticals (since July 31), autos (25%), trucks (25%), buses (10%), softwood lumber (10%), and steel, aluminum and copper at full value of goods since April 6. Polysilicon tariffs start Dec. 4. New initial actions on wind turbines (Oct. 22) and robotics and industrial machinery (Oct. 28) have status reports due in April 2027.

Section 301 actions include 25% on Brazil (since July 22) and 10% or 12.5% country rates in a forced-labor action (since July 24), per Reed Smith. Grant Thornton notes the Court of International Trade ruled 2-1 on May 7 that the Section 122 tariffs exceeded the administration's authority, with relief limited to three plaintiffs; the government has appealed. Section 122 tariffs were set to expire July 24 unless Congress extended them.
money: Buying cars, trucks or machinery? Prices include tariffs; compare model-year inventory.
Businesses: map your suppliers against the list and ask about tariff-adjustment clauses in contracts.
Consumers: expect tariff costs to show up gradually in prices of appliances, tools and furniture.

sources.t: Trump 2.0 tariff tracker, Nov. 3 (Reed Smith)
The Trump administration's new tariff road map (Grant Thornton)

stories.headline: Furniture and Cabinet Tariffs Step Up on Jan. 1
stories.deck: Upholstered furniture goes from 25% to 30%; kitchen cabinets to 50%.
stories.summary: Furniture/cabinet duties rise Jan. 1; buying before can save.
paras: Section 232 tariffs on upholstered furniture and kitchen cabinets are 25% for most countries through Dec. 31, 2026, and rise to 30% and 50% respectively on Jan. 1, 2027, per the Nov. 3 Reed Smith tracker.

Grant Thornton's roadmap lists furniture among Section 232 tariffs already in effect at 25%. The tracker notes that some of its own dates are inconsistent, so confirm against Federal Register notices.
money: Planning a kitchen remodel? A cabinet order placed and delivered before the step-up could save money; ask about price locks.
Compare U.S.-made options, which avoid import duties.
Do not rush into financing; interest on a rushed purchase can cancel the savings.

sources.t: Trump 2.0 tariff tracker, Nov. 3 (Reed Smith)
The Trump administration's new tariff road map (Grant Thornton)

stories.headline: Retail Distress: Children's Place Shake-Up and Holiday-Season Bankruptcies
stories.deck: Chains are restructuring or liquidating as costs rise ahead of peak season.
stories.summary: Children's Place faces bankruptcy rumors; Gordon (Christmas Central) filed Sept. 18.
paras: Retail Dive reported on Nov. 6 a leadership shake-up at The Children's Place amid bankruptcy rumors; no filing was reported. Gordon Companies, which runs Christmas Central, filed for Chapter 11 on Sept. 18 ahead of peak season, and Francesca's liquidation plan was confirmed Sept. 9. Sleep Number filed in June and agreed to a merger deal.

D & A Mattress, a 15-store El Paso and Las Cruces retailer, filed for Chapter 11 on Nov. 2, according to WhatNow; the petition gave no reason and Chapter 11 does not necessarily mean closure. Retail Dive's front page showed no other October-November filings, so the picture may be incomplete.
money: Use gift cards and store credit quickly if a retailer looks shaky; they can be worth little in bankruptcy.
Credit-card purchases get chargeback protection if goods are not delivered.
Liquidation sales are often not true discounts; compare prices.

sources.t: Distressed Retail (Retail Dive)
15-location mattress retailer files for Chapter 11 (WhatNow)

stories.headline: Home Insurance: FAIR Plan Rates Rise 29.1% for Renewals Since Oct. 15
stories.deck: More than 675,000 customers are affected; some in high-wildfire-risk areas could see wildfire premiums double.
stories.summary: FAIR Plan +29.1% average from Oct. 15; compare private quotes.
paras: California's FAIR Plan raised rates an average of 29.1% for renewals on or after Oct. 15, 2026, the largest increase in recent history, KQED reported. It affects more than 675,000 customers. The Plan had requested 35.8%. Drivers include 2025 Los Angeles wildfire losses and higher reinsurance costs.

A Stanford study cited by KQED found statewide premiums up 84% since 2020. FAIR Plan share of homes rose from under 2% to 5%, while new business is down 25% from a year ago. A broker said more traditional insurers are writing policies again.
money: Get quotes from private insurers and compare them against the FAIR Plan, including a combined FAIR Plan plus difference-in-conditions option.
Reduce risk with wildfire mitigation steps; some insurers discount for them.
Review dwelling coverage limits yearly so you are not underinsured.

sources.t: California FAIR Plan announces 29.1% rate hike (KQED)
California FAIR Plan rate hikes in 2026 (CoverageCat)

stories.headline: L.A. Rent Rules: Annual Caps Between 1% and 4% on About 650,000 Units
stories.deck: The City Council's rent-stabilization changes tie increases to inflation within a 1%-4% band and remove utility add-ons.
stories.summary: RSO caps 1-4%; utility add-ons removed.
paras: The Los Angeles City Council voted 12-2 to change the Rent Stabilization Ordinance, setting a 1% floor and 4% ceiling on annual increases for roughly 650,000 units built on or before Oct. 1, 1978. Increases use 90% of CPI. Prior caps ranged from 3% to 8%, plus 1-2% for utilities, which could total about 10%. Extra increases for landlords who pay utilities and for tenants with extra dependents are eliminated.
Officials also committed to seek funding for repairs for owners of 2-10 units and commissioned a study of effects on construction. Landlord groups argue the caps are below inflation and costs.
money: Tenants: confirm whether your unit is covered by the RSO and check increase notices against the allowed cap.
Small landlords: ask about repair funding for 2-10 unit buildings.

Renters in units outside the RSO may fall under California's AB 1482, which allows increases of 5% plus regional CPI up to a 10% maximum; check which law covers you. Newer buildings and some single-family homes may be exempt from both.

sources.t: LA City Council approves proposal on major rent changes (ABC7)
Los Angeles sets new 1% to 4% cap on RSO rent increases (Barnes & Thornburg)

stories.headline: California Minimum Wage Hits $17.40 and a Wave of Workplace Laws Arrives Jan. 1
stories.deck: The overtime-exempt salary threshold rises to $72,384; new rules cover AI layoffs notices, surveillance and arbitration.
stories.summary: Min. wage $17.40; exempt salary $72,384; AI-layoff Cal/WARN disclosure.
paras: California's statewide minimum wage rises to $17.40 an hour on Jan. 1, 2027, and the minimum salary for overtime-exempt workers rises to $72,384, per a Faegre Drinker summary of new laws. Many cities and counties set higher local minimums.

Other changes effective Jan. 1: Cal/WARN layoff notices must disclose layoffs caused by AI or automation (SB 951), employers may not use AI to detect emotions, and stay-or-pay contract limits take effect for new contracts. Limits on automated decision systems in employment begin July 1, 2027.
money: Employees: check whether your pay is at least the new floor and, if exempt, above $72,384.
Employers: update payroll and postings before Jan. 1.
If you are laid off, ask whether AI or automation was a cause; that disclosure is now required in notices.

sources.t: New California laws for 2027 (Faegre Drinker)
Minimum wage to increase to $17.40 on Jan. 1, 2027 (California DIR)

stories.headline: AI's Electric Bill: Data Centers Drive Grid Costs While Politics Turn Against Them
stories.deck: On the largest U.S. grid, capacity costs reached about $16.4 billion, with data centers estimated at 38%.
stories.summary: PJM capacity cost $16.4B, data centers ~38%; midterm politics target data centers.
paras: In the PJM grid serving about 67 million people, the capacity auction cleared at $325 per megawatt-day, about $16.4 billion in total; the market monitor estimated data centers account for roughly $6.3 billion, or 38%. Without a price cap, PJM said the price would have been $554.72, per Axios in July.

Politics are shifting: Open magazine reports that a Texas governor's candidate who campaigned for a pause on new data centers won, and investors fear tighter rules and local opposition over power and water use. One analyst said 10% of data centers may not happen under a Democratic Senate.
money: Ask your utility about time-of-use plans and energy efficiency programs if your bills are rising.
Investors: power-equipment and utility stocks can be volatile; GE Vernova fell 7.5% Thursday.
Check local utility rate cases that could pass data-center costs to households.

sources.t: AI continues to pressure power prices (Axios)
Why the Nasdaq fell 5.5% (Open magazine)
US markets rise as Democrats sweep midterm elections (Al Jazeera)

stories.headline: AI and Jobs: Information-Sector Employment Is Down 4.2% in a Year
stories.deck: The data show where jobs changed, not why; California now requires layoff notices to disclose AI causes.
stories.summary: Information jobs down 119,000 (-4.2%) y/y; Cal/WARN to disclose AI layoffs.
paras: Information-sector employment was 2.734 million in October, down 119,000 or 4.2% from a year earlier, while total payrolls rose 0.6%, per a FourWeekMBA analysis of BLS data. Data processing and hosting jobs were down 5.4% on the year. The article stresses the BLS release does not say AI caused the changes.
In California, SB 951 starts Jan. 1 and requires Cal/WARN layoff notices to disclose layoffs caused by AI or automation.
money: Build skills that pair with AI tools; employers are paying for people who use them.
If your role is exposed, build a six-month emergency fund.
Know your rights: Cal/WARN notice rules protect advance notice.

sources.t: Payrolls rose 165,000; information jobs fell 4.2% in a year (FourWeekMBA)
New California laws for 2027 (Faegre Drinker)

stories.headline: Up to $3,500 Off Your First Electric Vehicle, Applied at the Dealership
stories.deck: California's instant rebate cuts $3,500 for new ZEVs up to $50,000 and $1,750 for used ones up to $25,000.
stories.summary: $3,500 new / $1,750 used first-ZEV rebate at purchase.
paras: California's first-EV rebate is applied at the dealership: $3,500 for new zero-emission vehicles with an MSRP up to $50,000 and $1,750 for used ZEVs sold up to $25,000 through manufacturers' pre-owned programs, with no application or waiting, per the governor's office. The state's $135.5 million is matched by automakers.

Participating brands launched in stages starting in August; Mitsubishi was due in November, with Nissan and Volvo to be determined at the time of the announcement. The governor said nearly 12,000 people had used the rebate by mid-October. State funding is $135.5 million, matched by automakers for about $271 million combined. The coverage read for this edition lists no end date or income limit, so confirm details with the dealer or program page.
money: Ask the dealer to confirm the rebate before signing.
Compare with federal credits and utility EV rates.
Include charging and insurance in the cost.

sources.t: Governor announces $3,500 instant rebates for first ZEV buyers (Gov. of California)
Nearly 12,000 Californians switch to EVs thanks to MyFirstEV rebate (electrive)

stories.headline: Social Security Rises 3.6% in January; Medicare Premium Will Take a Bite
stories.deck: The average increase is about $75 a month; the wage cap rises to $192,300.
stories.summary: COLA 3.6% (~$75/mo); Part B projected $209.50.
paras: Social Security announced a 3.6% cost-of-living increase for 2027, the largest since 2023, about $75 a month for the average beneficiary. Notices go out starting in early December. The maximum earnings subject to Social Security tax rises to $192,300 from $184,500.
Medicare Part B is usually deducted from the check; trustees project a rise of $6.60 to $209.50 in 2027, which would leave most with a net increase of at least 3%.

AARP adds that the earnings test before full retirement age withholds $1 for every $2 earned above $25,560, up from $24,480, and the substantial gainful activity limit for SSDI rises to $1,770 a month.
money: Check your December notice for the exact net amount.
Budget for Part B and drug costs; compare Medicare plans during open enrollment.
Low-income seniors may qualify for Medi-Cal and Medicare Savings Programs.

sources.t: Social Security says retirees will get a 3.6% raise for 2027 (Honolulu Star-Advertiser)
Social Security changes for 2027 (AARP)
